newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia reports surge in foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Colombia reports surge in foreign investment.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Colombia excluding the oil sector jumped 41 percent in July over the same month last year, the Colombian investment board Coinvertir said in its most recent report on foreign investment flows into the country.

It said the surge in July -- which followed negative growth in May and June -- pushed total direct foreign investment in Colombia, excluding the volatile oil sector, up four percent during the first seven months of the year compared to the same period in 1995.
The healthy increase in July came despite an 85 percent drop in foreign portfolio investment during the month compared to July 1995, according to Coinvertir.
It said flagging investment in equities was compensated with a large increase in foreign flows into the manufacturing and industrial sectors.

Traditionally, 25 percent of direct foreign investment excluding oil is channeled into portfolios and and 75 percent into business and industry. But in July, the mix changed to seven percent in portfolios and 93 percent into industry and manufacturing.
Convertir said Panama, the Virgin Islands and Cayman Islands were jointly responsible for 42 percent of direct foreign investment in July while the United States accounted for just 16 percent.

It added that countries including Canada, Liechtenstein, Uruguay and Hong Kong, which traditionally showed little investor interest in Colombia, had begun to demonstrate more interest and that Europe and Central America -- jointly responsible for 54 percent of foreign investment so far this year -- had also increased their presence in Colombia.
